                    ### Question
                    Which of the following characteristics will a patient with helminth infection and one who is responding to an allergen have in common ?:

                    ### Options
                    opa. In both patients an increase of cytotoxic T lymphocytes will be detected.
opb. In both patients the innate immunity will be deficient.
opc. In both, an elevated level of serum IgE will be detected.
opd. Both patients have a high risk of developing an autoimmune disease.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Patients with helminth infections and those responding to allergens share a common characteristic of elevated serum IgE levels. Helminth infections typically trigger a Th2 immune response, leading to increased production of IgE antibodies, which is also a hallmark of allergic reactions. Therefore, both conditions are associated with elevated IgE levels. The reasoning regarding cytotoxic T lymphocytes and innate immunity deficiency is not supported by consensus, as helminth infections do not necessarily lead to a deficiency in innate immunity, and the role of cytotoxic T lymphocytes is not central to either condition. Additionally, while both conditions can involve immune dysregulation, the link to autoimmune diseases is not definitively established. Thus, the most accurate conclusion is that both conditions exhibit elevated serum IgE levels.
